`return` inside the clause that runs on the way out it replaces whatever the block was leaving with, so a failure raised in the body disappears and nothing anywhere records that it happened Fix: move it after the block, so what the block was leaving with survives

Calls itself 1 times per invocation with no memo in sight. there is nothing that can stop it, so the first call takes the stack down with it Fix: give `loops` the case that answers without calling itself

`rows` is changed while it is being walked. the walk and the change disagree about what is left, so elements are skipped or seen twice depending on where the change landed Fix: collect what to change, and change it after the walk
`case 1:` runs on into the arm below the arm below runs too, and nothing written here says whether that was wanted or forgotten Fix: end the arm, or say in the code that falling through is the point

`(kind === "a")` is asked twice in one chain the second arm cannot be reached, so whatever it was written to do has never run and nobody has noticed Fix: decide which of the two arms was meant, and delete the other

Both arms of this branch do the same thing. the decision changes nothing, so either it is not a decision or one arm was meant to differ and does not Fix: keep one body and delete the branch, or make the arms differ

`count` is compared against itself. the answer is decided before it runs, so either the comparison does nothing or one side was meant to be something else Fix: one side was meant to be something else; decide which

`found = a + b` assigns where a condition is expected. it reads as a comparison and behaves as a write, which is why it is the typo that survives review Fix: assign above the branch, or compare if that is what was meant

This catch clause has an empty body. the failure is swallowed silently, so the first sign of it is wrong data somewhere far away with nothing in the logs to connect the two Fix: log it, rethrow it, or write the reason ignoring it is correct

This statement cannot run: the block always returns before reaching it. this code cannot run, so whatever it was meant to do is not happening and has not been happening Fix: delete it, or move it above the exit if it was meant to run

`loadOne` answers later and nothing takes the answer. nothing waits for it and nothing hears if it fails, so the failure arrives somewhere with no idea what asked for it Fix: wait for it, or say in the code who is going to

`expect(add(1, 1)).toBe(add(1, 1));` has the same expression on both sides it holds the code to whatever the code already does, so it passes through every change including the one that breaks it Fix: write the answer the test expects, not the call that produces it

`RegExp` runs on every pass of the loop. the same pattern is parsed and compiled on every pass when once would do, and compiling is the expensive half of matching Fix: compile it once above the loop and reuse it

Declared with `skip`. a skipped test is a question nobody answered; it reports green forever while the behaviour it named goes unchecked Fix: fix it and re-enable it, or delete it and record the question it was asking

Parameter `total` is reassigned inside the function. the caller's value changes without the call site saying so, which is the hardest kind of change to find when it turns out to be wrong Fix: assign to a local instead of `total`, and return the result

Parameter `value` is reassigned inside the function. the caller's value changes without the call site saying so, which is the hardest kind of change to find when it turns out to be wrong Fix: assign to a local instead of `value`, and return the result

`rqx-ignore with no reason` turns off a check that covers this code. the waiver is refused and the finding still stands, because a waiver nobody has to justify is how a rule gets switched off one line at a time Fix: say why the finding is acceptable here, or fix it

the handler is only `throw error;` it reads as a decision about the failure and makes none, while costing the stack trace in the languages that rebuild one on the way out Fix: delete the handler and let it propagate, or add what this level knows about the failure

`warmTheCache` runs when the file is loaded. it happens before any caller has asked for anything, in whatever order the imports happen to resolve, and nothing can stop it Fix: put it behind a function the caller chooses to call

`CsvWriter` is built by the object that holds it. nothing can be put in its place, so every test of the owner stands up the real collaborator and everything behind it Fix: accept it as an argument, so a caller can decide what it is
